topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer biology course, outlines the multidisciplinary audience, and presents the core learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Genetic Regulation and Differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises from accumulating genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal tissue differentiation programs and discuss the challenges of modeling this complex architecture in vitro.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Stepwise Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between benign and malignant tumors through histopathological evidence of basement membrane invasion, metastatic dissemination, and adenoma-to-carcinoma progression.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature and Pathophysiological Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the standard naming conventions for different tumor classes and describe the physiological mechanisms by which neoplastic growths cause severe morbidity and death.

topics.label: Tumor Incidence Across Humans and Other Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey cancer frequency and mortality trends in human populations and demonstrate how cancer acts as a universal disease of multicellular development across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Modalities of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale, histological foundations, and comparative efficacy of screening programs for early cancer detection across different tissue sites.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session by reinforcing the learning outcomes and providing logistical instructions for upcoming practicals.
